row.name: The Full Ridge
row.overview: Climbs the northeast ridge of Basin from its toe, then follows the sawtooth back to the Humphreys Basin high point. Go down to Horton, or keep circling Four Gables to complete the cirque. The start is a long approach, gaining thousands of feet up a sagebrush slope. Lower towers are adventurous and need involved navigation; some are climbed over, others bypassed, and rock quality varies. The skyline sawtooth is mostly talus up to Basin's top. Basin's western high point needs scrambling at third and fourth class. A grade is hard to assign; expect an adventure.
row.approach: Start at the Horton Lakes trailhead, reached by a four-wheel-drive road from Buttermilk Road. The route begins at the toe of the northeast ridge of Basin Mountain, reached by a long climb up the sagebrush slope from the trailhead. The lower ridge has a series of towers, some best climbed over and others bypassed, with complicated route-finding.

row.name: Direct East Face
row.overview: Ten pitches directly up the middle of Four Gables South (Peak 12,801'), on the east side. Rock is grainy and loose. Pitches 1-4 are easy and simul-climbed, about 500'. Sandy ledges and cracks form the 200' fifth (5.10-). Hardest is the 150' sixth pitch, 5.10+: corner crack, then a roof that is strenuous. The seventh, 5.10 and 100', passes stacked blocks that are serious: push softly, never pull, since the belayer stands directly below. Pitches 8-9, about 250' at 5.6, reach a cave; a tunnel then leads out for the 5.7 final pitch of 100'.

row.name: East Ridge from Piute Pass
row.description: Hike over Piute Pass, cross Humphreys Basin to the saddle on the east ridge, then scramble boulders to the summit.

row.name: 7th Gable, or Spiral Ridge
row.overview: Follow cracks to a slight chimney or gully, which gives access to the narrow spiraling ridge that leads to the apparent summit. From the gully, undercling a flake for a high reach (5.10-) and continue upward. Stay on the ridge. About two thirds of the way up is a fairly blank section of slab moves and a mantel. One pitch below the apparent top, trend right onto the steep face, on chunky cracks.
row.approach: From the east, begin at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail beyond Upper Pine Lake, branching toward Honeymoon Lake. Carry on through Granite Park to the crest, which you cross at Granite Bear Pass, south of Italy Pass beside Granite Park Spire. Go west cross-country into the Bear Lakes area, passing Big Bear Lake on its north and Little Bear Lake on its south, then trend southwest past tarns to Vee Lake. Walk down its outlet to the East Fork of Bear Creek and work uphill cross-country to the peak. The route is the leftmost gable on the north face.

row.name: Via Sallie Keyes Lakes
row.description: Hike the trail around Florence Lake and across the San Joaquin, take the cutoff use trail toward Selden Pass, and climb to Sallie Keyes Lakes. Continue over boulders and a bench below the summit; the final slopes are easier than they look.

row.name: Southwest Ridge via Tombstone Pass
row.description: Follow Tombstone Creek to Tombstone Pass, traverse to the cirque below the summit and climb the southwest ridge to the summit block. The block itself is a short 5.4 crack on the south side. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

row.name: Direct North Buttress
row.overview: A varied mix of cracks and faces. Heading left along a ledge below an orange lichen bulge leads to the "Triple Cracks", which seemed the hardest physically; the alcove has loose rock beneath it, yet the narrow crack over it is solid. Farther up, a 5.10b dihedral begins stiff before easing, and a big fixed cam sits in the offwidth/chimney past it. Near the top, gendarmes and pillars crowd a ridge where 4th and 5th class mix.

row.name: East Pinnacle
row.overview: Beside Merriam Peak, this climb surprised the party with steep, engaging pitches alternating with exposed ridge traverses instead of easy scrambling. It is better with minimal beta for each pitch. Difficulties generally go via clean steep cracks or by escaping right. A clean offwidth splitter on the fourth pitch merits a go if you carry big cams (a #5 and #4 likely enough); the party instead found good climbing to the right, which curved back left to top out above it. The last chimney exit is novel.
row.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, follow the trail past Pine Lake and Upper Pine Lake to Honeymoon Lake, then continue to Granite Park. Above the lake, cut southwest cross-country up and over Royce Pass to reach the Royce Lakes basin. The route begins at the toe of the large pinnacle and ridge on the east side of Royce, an easy walk from Merriam Peak; it climbs the ridge on the east face of the nearly detached spire that rises over Royce Lake.
